source_title: Barbara Barrie Made Her Final Public Appearance Over 1 Year Before Ending Her Life by Medical Aid - People.com
source_excerpt:
Barbara Barrie died at 95 on Wednesday, Oct. 28
Tommy McArdle is a Writer-Reporter on the Movies team at PEOPLE. He joined the brand in 2022.
Barbara Barrie seemingly made her final public appearance at the March 2025 world premiere for the play We Had a World in New York City
Barrie died at 95 on Wednesday, Oct. 28
The acclaimed stage and screen actress was nominated for a Tony Award for her performance in the original production of Company and received an Academy Award nomination in 1980 for Breaking Away
Barbara Barrie last appeared in public at a premiere for a play in New York City over one year before she died at 95.
The acclaimed actress, a Tony Award and Oscar nominee, died on Wednesday, Oct. 28 at her Manhattan home following a terminal cancer diagnosis, The New York Times reported. Her daughter, Jane Harnick, said her mother’s death was medically assisted.
Barrie’s final public outings included an appearance at the December 2021 opening night for the revival of Company on Broadway. (She originated the role of Sarah in the original 1970 Broadway production, earning a Tony Award nomination for Best Featured Actress in a Musical for her performance.) The actress joined other Broadway luminaries at the November 2023 tribute to the famed lyricist and her late brother-in-law, Sheldon Harnick.
In March 2025, Barrie stepped out for the world premiere of We Had a World in New York City, per BroadwayWorld . At that event, she posed for photos with the play’s star Joanna Gleason, director Trip Cullman and playwright Joshua Harmon. The Private Benjamin actress was also snapped with Marvin’s Room director Anne Kauffman and stage star Lindsay Mendez .
Barrie was born Barbara Berman in Chicago on May 23, 1931. Her family moved to Corpus Christi, Texas, and she attended Del Mar College, where she majored in journalism, but quickly became interested in acting. She didn’t think the transition was strange. “After all, they’re both creative,” she told the Akron Beacon Journal in 1963.
Barrie made her Broadway debut in The Wooden Dish in 1955. In 1959, she appeared in The Beaux’ Stratagem , and in 1966, she starred in Happily Never After .
Barrie’s film debut was in 1956’s Giant , a role that came about because she was visiting her family when the movie was shooting in Corpus Christi. But her most significant early career success came on television. Her many TV roles in the ‘50s and ‘60s included episodes of The Defenders , Route 66 , Naked City , Dr. Kildare , The Twilight Zone , The Alfred Hitchcock Hour and The Fugitive .
Barrie’s first big film role was in 1964’s One Potato, Two Potato . The film depicted an interracial relationship between Barrie, a divorcée, and a man she meets at work, played by Bernie Hamilton, who was Black. Barrie won the Best Actress award at the Cannes Film Festival for the movie.
Over the course of Barrie’s career, she earned an Oscar nomination for Best Supporting Actress for her work in 1979’s Breaking Away and also notably starred in television series like Barney Miller and Suddenly Susan .
Her last movie roles came in the 2023 film The Magnificent Meyersons and 2025’s Things Like This . She last appeared on Broadway in the 2017 play Significant Other , which was written by Harmon.

In 1964, she married actor, director and producer Jay Harnick. They had two children, Jane, born in 1965, and Aaron, born in 1969.
Barrie’s love for her husband, who died in 2007, and children ran deep. When she discussed the musical Company with Playbill in 1970, she said, “I’m very boring about my children. They give me such joy that’s all I talk about.”
Barrie is survived by her two children.
